name: Cholamandalam Investment & Finance Company Ltd
about: Cholamandalam Investment & Finance Company is one of the premier diversified non-banking finance companies in India, engaged in providing vehicle finance, home loans and Loan against property. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 26.6% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 28.0%.
Revenue growth accelerated from 17% to 24% YoY over the last 4 quarters.

cash.note: For lenders, operating cash flow mostly reflects loan-book growth; cash conversion isn't a meaningful test.

ledger.quote: our objective was to deliver around 25% growth
ledger.statement: Full-year FY27 growth of around 25%, guidance held (not raised)
ledger.speaker: Viral Shah
ledger.evidence: Q2 FY27 AUM grew 25% YoY to INR2,68,009 crore on 47% disbursement growth (C1), in line with the target. The ledger calls this guidance 'held', but it is above the 20-23% (G17) and 22-23% (G11) given on the two prior calls, so in practice it was raised.

ledger.speaker: Ravindra Kundu

context.speaker: Vellayan Subbiah
context.text: Thank you, Nischint, and thank you, Kotak, for hosting this call. Good evening, everyone. I'm happy to take you through our performance for Q2 FY27. We continued to witness strong momentum across our lending businesses during the quarter with broad-based growth across vehicle finance, SME and consumer finance. Aggregate disbursements grew by 47% year-on-year to INR35,872 crores, reflecting healthy demand conditions, execution strength and continued expansion of our distribution franchise. This translated into an AUM of INR2,68,009 crores, registering a growth of 25% year-on-year. In vehicle finance, industry volumes remained robust across key segments, supported by replacement demand, improving economic activity and healthy freight utilization. We are particularly pleased that Chola continued to grow materially ahead of the industry, driven by market share gains, deep customer engagement, strong dealer relationships and disciplined execution on the ground. Vehicle finance disbursements grew by 31% year-on-year to INR17,801 crores, resulting in an AUM of INR1,29,787 crores, a growth of 21% year-on-year. The secured SME finance business across all key product lines, including LAP, SME and SBPL continued its strong growth trajectory for the quarter with disbursements increasing by 42% year-on-year to INR9,345 crores. This growth was driven by our focused market penetration strategy, strong on-ground execution and deep engagement with channel partners. We witnessed consistent growth across all product lines, resulting in an overall AUM growth of 27% year-on-year to INR72,356 crores with LAP at INR57,447 crores, a growth of 24%, SME at INR10,943 crores, a growth of 45% and SBPL at INR3,966 crores, a growth of 35%. This reflects both the scalability of the franchise and incre

context.speaker: Viral Shah
context.text: And on the related point, Vellayan, I think you also rightfully pointed out the consumer business that has been kind of scaling up now. It is almost 3 quarters wherein now we are seeing that the PBT, ROTA is now consistently crossing, say, 3%, 3.5% kind of a mark. And still, I think this is not the optimal profitability for the sub-segment given that there are various other sub- segments that are folded into this segment that we see over here.

context.speaker: Can you -
context.text: or rather, would you like to throw some light in terms of some of the sub-segments, consumer durable, mobile, PL? And what could be the, say, optimal profitability looking like over here from a medium-term perspective? Ravindra Kundu: Currently, CSEL comprises two key business segments: Unsecured Business Loans, Personal Loans and Professional Loans, and Consumer Durables (mobile and non-mobile) along with Digital Lending. These businesses are led by Sucheth Bharathan and Vijay Kini, respectively. As these businesses continue to scale and attain meaningful size, we intend to present their performance separately. By the time we begin disclosing them independently, we expect both businesses to demonstrate strong profitability metrics. They are already delivering a pre-tax ROA of around 3.6%, and we Page 4 of 23 Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Limited October 28, 2026 believe that, on a combined basis, they have the potential to sustainably deliver over 4% pre-tax ROA. The key driver of further improvement will be the reduction in net credit costs, along with some moderation in operating expenses. While we are not disclosing segment-wise financials at this stage, we remain confident that, together, these businesses can comfortably deliver a pre-tax ROA in excess of 4% over the medium term. The underlying business economics remain strong, and we expect profitability to improve further as the portfolios mature and operating leverage continues to play out.

The Consumer segment delivered 45% year-on-year disbursement growth, driven by sustained momentum across product segments with the newly launched Gold Loan business disbursing INR1,130 crores in Q4 FY'26. Home loan disbursements saw mild moderation in Q4 due to procedural timing factors, including election-related administrative slowdowns, land-record digitization mismatches, and localized lien- marking delays in select markets, which temporarily extended verification and disbursal timelines. Consumer segment AUM grew at 20% year-on-year, including 23% in Home Loans while CSEL AUM increased 4% despite the exit from partnership-led businesses.

As mentioned in the opening note, and as the Chairman highlighted earlier, there has been some delay in completing documentation due to the ongoing elections in two southern states. This has temporarily impacted disbursements in both LAP and Home Loans. However, this has not affected our overall asset growth. We remain confident of achieving asset growth of 25% or higher in the Home Loan and LAP businesses. In addition, our other mortgage segments—SBPL and SME—are expected to grow at a rate exceeding 30%. Taken together, growth in the mortgage businesses will continue to be the primary driver of overall company growth.

Historically, this has been in the range of 1% to 1.2% but redefining a steady-state level will take time. Once all eight businesses are fully scaled and stabilized—over the next one to two years—we will be in a much better position to clearly define our long-term ROA and net credit loss levels. For now, we are comfortable holding our guidance at 1.5% for the current financial year, while continuing to work toward further improvement.

On the vehicle finance side, the credit costs have stabilized, and we are looking at a reasonable moderation in Q4. ROA for Q3 FY '26 stands at 3.2% and ROE at 19.11%. With the second half progressing well, we anticipate Q4 to reflect improved performance in line with past trends. In terms of liquidity and capital adequacy, we hold a strong liquidity position with total liquid assets of INR18,857 crores, including undrawn sanction lines. The ALM is comfortable with no negative cumulative mismatches across all time buckets. Our capital adequacy position stood at 19.16% in December '25 with Tier 1 capital at 14.12%.

business.what_it_does: Non-bank lender to retail and small-business borrowers, in three areas: vehicle finance; secured SME lending (LAP, SME and SBPL); and consumer lending, which covers home loans, CSEL (unsecured business, personal and professional loans, consumer durables and digital lending) and a new gold-loan book. AUM was INR2,68,009 crore at Q2 FY27, up 25% YoY.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Growth is broad-based across vehicle finance, SME and consumer, and running ahead of plan (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: AUM grew 25% YoY and vehicle-finance AUM 21%. Revenue growth accelerated every quarter, from 17.3% to 23.8%, and PAT rose 40.5%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Credit costs are falling, from a 1.5% guide to ~1.4% (G16, G2, C6).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Margin at 23.6% against 20.9% a year earlier, and PAT growing 16.7 points faster than revenue, fit that story. But the margin is still 570bps below three years ago, and the H1 credit-cost figure itself is not in the inputs.
Q2 disbursements grew 47%, but October was guided at only ~18% (G7). Whether 25% AUM growth holds if H2 disbursement growth runs near that pace can't be tested from the inputs yet.

bull.point: The growth guide was raised twice and is being met: FY27 guidance went from 20-23% to 22-23% to ~25%, and Q2 FY27 AUM grew 25% to INR2,68,009 crore on 47% disbursement growth.
Profit is outgrowing the book: PAT rose 40.5% YoY against revenue growth of 23.8%, the margin was 23.6% against 20.9% a year earlier, and the credit-cost guide was cut from 1.5% to 1.4%.
ROE is 19.0%, and CSEL's ~3.6% pre-tax ROA already beats its 3.5% FY27 target, with more than 4% guided for the medium term.

bear.point: Funding costs are rising faster than guided: the expected cost-of-funds increase went from ~10bps in H2 (Q1 FY27 call) to ~20bps (Q2 FY27 call), while NIM is guided flat at ~8%.
Growth is consuming capital: D/E is 6.72 on INR2,31,911 crore of borrowings, and the board has approved raising up to INR5,000 crore.
Momentum may fade: October disbursements were guided at ~18% against 47% in Q2. The 3-year PAT CAGR of 25.2% trails the revenue CAGR of 34.2%, and the margin is 570bps below three years ago.

questions: October disbursement growth was guided at ~18% against 47% in Q2. What was the actual figure, which products slowed, and what H2 disbursement growth does the ~25% AUM target assume?
The expected H2 cost-of-funds rise doubled from ~10bps to ~20bps in one quarter. What drove it, and what FY27 NIM does it leave against the ~8% guide?
What were H1 FY27 net credit cost and CSEL credit loss against the 1.4% and sub-5% targets, and at what Tier 1 level would you draw on the INR5,000 crore raise?
